rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes their challenge as demanding the punishment Lot had threatened, implying that he warned them of it.
rows.anchor: أي فيما تعدنا من نزول العذاب على ما في الكشاف وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading makes them challenge Lot's implied claim that their conduct deserved punishment, conveyed by his reproachful question.
rows.anchor: في دعوى استحقاقنا العذاب على ما نحن عليه المفهومة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading makes their reply challenge Lot's assertion that the conduct he censured was reprehensible.
rows.anchor: في دعوى استقباح ذلك الناطق بها كلامك

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan, followed by Abu al-Su'ud, places this answer at Lot's first admonition and the expulsion answer in al-A'raf and al-Naml later, so the exclusive formulations do not conflict.
rows.anchor: قاله أبو حيان وتبعه أبو السعود وتعقب بأن هذا التعيين يحتاج إلى توقيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chronological account is challenged for lacking transmitted evidence; its defense is that mockery suits early admonition, while expulsion suits later retaliation after repeated reproach.
rows.anchor: من باب التكذيب والسخرية وهو أوفق بأوائل المواعظ والتوبيخات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reconciliation says this answer responds to Lot's counsel, whereas the expulsion answer records what his people said among themselves while deliberating.
rows.anchor: إن ما هنا جواب قومه عليه السلام له إذ نصحهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reconciliation assigns the two answers to different groups, one to the chiefs and the other to everyone else.
rows.anchor: إن أحد الجوابين صدر عن كبار قومه وامرائهم والآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some eminent commentators appear to choose that each exclusive answer is relative to the response Lot hoped to receive when calling them to follow him.
rows.anchor: يقتضي اختيار أن يكون كل من الحصرين بالاضافة إلى الجواب

words: ٱتْلُ مَآ أُوحِىَ إِلَيْكَ مِنَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Continue reciting revelation to draw near to God, recall its meanings, remind people, and urge them to follow its rulings, manners, and virtues.
rows.anchor: أي دم على تلاوة ذلك تقربا إلى الله تعالى بتلاوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Establish prayer means maintain it; it encompasses the prescribed congregational prayers, and the Prophet's command also directs his community.
rows.anchor: أي داوم على إقامتها وحيث كانت الصلاة منتظمة للصوات المكتوبة

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنكَرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer deters through its acts of worship and embodied humility: its words and postures admonish the worshipper against disobeying the Lord whose greatness they express.
rows.anchor: لتضمنها صنوف العبادة من التكبير والتسبيح والقراءة والوقوف بين يدي الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not promise every person who prays will stop sinning: divine prohibition also fails to ensure universal abstention, so warning need not entail compliance.
rows.anchor: ليس نهي الصلاة بأعظم من نهيه سبحانه وتعالى فإذا لم يكن هناك استلزام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، والكلبي، وابن كريج، وحماد بن أبي سليمان
rows.claim: They say prayer restrains the worshipper from indecency and wrong only while he performs it, when its admonitory words and actions are present.
rows.anchor: ونقل أبو حيان عن ابن عباس والكلبي وابن كريج وحماد بن أبي سليمان

rows.speaker: القطب
rows.claim: Al-Qutb says prayer is for God's remembrance (20:14), which inhibits displeasing acts; a sinner who prays would sin more without prayer, an explanation the author views skeptically.
rows.anchor: أن الصلاة تقام لذكر الله تعالى كما قال عز من قائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes prayer as a cause of abstention, not a universal guarantee: an indefinite noun in an affirmative statement need not apply to every case.
rows.anchor: إن المراد أن الصلاة سبب للانتهاء عن ذلك وليس هذا كليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deterrence varies with prayer's quality: complete, attentive prayer restrains strongly, while heedless, deficient prayer barely restrains and is rejected like a worn garment cast back at its owner.
rows.anchor: النهي الذي ذكرناه يتفاوت بحسب تفاوت أداء الصلاة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: A report from Abu Abd Allah says acceptance can be assessed by whether prayer kept its performer from indecency and wrong; acceptance is proportionate to its restraint.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه قال :

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Al-Hasan transmits the Prophet's saying that prayer which fails to restrain from indecency and wrong is no prayer; another wording says it increases distance from God.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم من لم تنهه صلاته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report traced to Ibn Abbas as a Prophetic narration gives the wording that prayer which fails to restrain its performer only increases his distance from God.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما مرفوعا

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: When told a man prayed at length, Ibn Masud replied that prayer benefits only one who obeys it, then recited the verse.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that when told a man prays at night but steals in the morning, the Prophet said prayer would stop him.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله تعالى عنه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report says an Anṣārī youth who prayed with the Prophet yet committed indecencies soon repented after the Prophet said prayer would restrain him; Ibn Hajar says he could not find this in hadith books.
rows.anchor: إلا أن ابن حجر ذكر فيه أنه لم يجده في كتب الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning is canonical prayer, supported by sound reports; Quran and supplication readings lack a reason to depart from that sense.
rows.anchor: حمل الصلاة في الآية على الصلاة المعروفة هو الظاهر المؤيد

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar transmits that prayer here means the Quran.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنهما أن المراد بها هنا القرآن

rows.speaker: ابن بحر
rows.claim: Ibn Bahr interprets prayer as الدعاء, calling people to God's command, which restrains from indecency and wrong.
rows.anchor: إن المراد بها الدعاء أي أقم الدعاء إلى أمر الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas read that prayer commands right conduct and forbids indecency and wrong.
rows.anchor: عن الربيع بن أنس أنه كان يقرأ

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، وابن مسعود، وابن عمر، وأبو قرة، ومجاهد، وعطية
rows.claim: They interpret the phrase as God's remembrance of people being greater than their remembrance of Him; Ibn Abbas also cites 2:152.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وابن مسعود وابن عمر وأبو قرة ومجاهد وعطية

rows.speaker: أبو مالك
rows.claim: Abu Malik says God's remembrance of the servant in prayer is greater than prayer; remembrance is annexed to its subject, with its object omitted.
rows.anchor: عن أبي مالك أنه قال ذكر الله تعالى العبد في الصلاة أكبر من الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading makes remembrance generally greater than everything.
rows.anchor: أي أكبر من كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other views say the worshipper's remembrance in prayer exceeds the other prayer pillars, remembrance outside prayer, or all other deeds.
rows.anchor: ولذكر العبد لله تعالى في الصلاة أكبر من سائر أركان الصلاة

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
rows.claim: Muadh says no human deed better saves from God's punishment than remembrance; he ranks it above fighting in God's path, even sword combat until the sword breaks.
rows.anchor: عن معاذ بن جبل قال : ما عمل آدمي

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Abu Darda calls remembrance the best, most beloved deed, higher in rank and better than fighting an enemy or giving money.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال : ألا أخبركم بخير أعمالكم

rows.speaker: سلمان
rows.claim: Asked which deed is best, Salman answers that nothing is better than remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: عن سلمان أنه سئل أي العمل أفضل قال : أما تقرأ القرآن

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء وسلمان
rows.claim: Al-Bahr also attributes the earlier view, that God's remembrance of people exceeds theirs of Him, to Abu Darda and Salman, perhaps reflecting alternate transmissions.
rows.anchor: ونسب في البحر إلى أبي الدرداء وسلمان رضي الله تعالى عنهما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says remembrance is greatest; mosque gatherings studying scripture are shaded by angels and God's guests, and seekers of knowledge are guided toward Paradise.
rows.anchor: عن عنترة قال : قلت لابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take remembrance to mean prayer, as in 62:9, and say prayer exceeds other acts because remembrance is central to its merit and restraint from sin.
rows.anchor: المراد بذكر الله الصلاة كما في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says remembering God's prohibition and threat at the moment of temptation deters more than prayer.
rows.anchor: ولذكر الله تعالى عند الفحشاء والمنكر وذكر نهيه عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On those readings remembrance is a verbal noun annexed to its object, with the comparative complement omitted; akbar may alternatively not be comparative.
rows.anchor: على هذه الأقوال مصدر مضاف للمفعول والمفضل عليه محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rewards good and obedience excellently; Abu Hayyan includes good and evil and says recompense brings promise, threat, and an exhortation to vigilance.
rows.anchor: من الخير والطاعة فيجازيكم بذلك أحسن المجازاة

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says God knows good and evil and recompenses accordingly, so the ending promises, threatens, and urges vigilance.
rows.anchor: من الخير والشر فيجازيكم بحسبه ففيه وعد ووعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God originates creation, restores it through resurrection, and all return to Him for recompense.
rows.anchor: ثم يعيده ( بالبعث ( ثم إليه ترجعون

rows.speaker: عبدالله وطلحة
rows.claim: Abdullah and Talha read the verb as يبديء, with a prefixed damma and kasra on the dal.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبدالله وطلحة ( يبديء ) بضم الياء وكسر الدال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting the destination conveys restriction; shifting from third-person narration to direct address confronts the polytheists with an intensified personal threat.
rows.anchor: وتقديم المعمول للتخصيص وكان الظاهر يرجعون بياء الغيبة

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وروح
rows.claim: Abu Amr and Rawh read يرجعون in third-person plural, as expected from the surrounding narration.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وروح ( يرجعون ) بياء الغيبة كما هو الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description is evidence of God's power, wisdom, and workmanship; it lays groundwork for monotheism and refutes and rebukes idolatry.
rows.anchor: استئناف جيء به للاستشهاد بما فصل فيه على عزته عزوجل التي هي كمال القدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عمد is the plural of عماد, like أهب is the plural of إهاب; it means supports, and the plural reflects the multiple heavens.
rows.anchor: والعمد جمع عماد كأهب جمع أهاب وهو ما يعمد به أي يسند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ترونها is an independent clause showing that if the heavens had supports, they would be visible; vision is visual, not intellectual.
rows.anchor: لأنها لو كانت لها عمد رؤيت فالجملة لا محل لها من الإعراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively ترونها qualifies supports: the heavens have invisible pillars, interpreted as pillars of divine power; this interpretation is reported from Mujahid.
rows.anchor: بغير عمد مرئية على التقييد للرمز إلى أنه تعالى عمدها بعمد لا ترى

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The interpretation of unseen supports is reported from Mujahid.
rows.anchor: عمدها بعمد لا ترى وهي عمد القدرة وروى ذلك عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that a perfect human in each age supports the heavens, which fold when humanity ends, has no basis in Quran or Sunna.
rows.anchor: ولذا إذا أنقطع الإنسان الكامل وذلك عند إنقطاع النوع الإنساني

words: وَأَلْقَىٰ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ رَوَٰسِىَ أَن تَمِيدَ بِكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God placed lofty or firmly fixed mountains so the earth would not sway; without them surrounding waters and necessary storm winds might make it shift.
rows.anchor: أي ألقى فيها جبالا شوامخ أو ثوابت كراهة ( أن تميد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some philosophers argue that on a spherical earth centered at the world's center of gravity, moving heavy objects could shift its center and move the earth, though imperceptibly because their mass is negligible.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر بعض الفلاسفة أنه يلزم بناء على كرية الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another suggestion is that without mountains, a large sea formed by flowing water and windblown sand and soil could shift the earth.
rows.anchor: يقول : لا يبعد حركة ثقيل عليها كماء جرى من مكان إلى آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not limit the wisdom of mountains to preventing sway; they have innumerable other purposes.
rows.anchor: ولا دلالة في الآية على إنحصار حكمة إلقاء الرواسي فيها بسلامتها عن الميد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author accepts a spherical earth, as held by al-Ghazali, and notes Ibn Abbas's report and philosophers' agreement; sense and inference support it.
rows.anchor: كما ذهب إليه الغزالي وكذا ذهب إلى كرية السماء وجاء في رواية عن إبن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not prove that the heavens are immobile, as followers of Pythagoras say; other doctrines behind that view are even more plainly false.
rows.anchor: لا دلالة فيها على عدم حركتها على الإستعارة دائما كما ذهب إليه أصحاب فيثاغورس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بث means bringing into existence and spreading; its root sense is stirring and dispersing, as in the images of scattered dust and dispersed moths.
rows.anchor: وأصل البث الإثارة والتفريق ومنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means every kind or species of animal.
rows.anchor: من كل نوع من أنواعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water is rain and heaven means the upper direction; it may mean the canopy by figurative interpretation, but that should not be adopted without compelling evidence against observation.
rows.anchor: هو المطر والمراد بالسماء جهة العلو

words: فَأَنۢبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍۢ كَرِيمٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Plants grow because of the rain; زوج means kind and كريم means noble or highly beneficial.
rows.anchor: كريم 01 أي شريف كثير المنفعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift to the first-person plural in both verbs highlights care: rain and growth recur and sustain animal life and the inhabited earth.
rows.anchor: والإلتفات إلى ضمير العظمة في الفعلين لإبراز مزيد الإعتناء بهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This refers to the heavens, earth, and other enumerated matters; خلق الله means God's created work.
rows.anchor: أي ما ذكر من السموات والأرض وسائر الأمور المعدودة

words: فَأَرُونِى مَاذَا خَلَقَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن دُونِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أروني means inform or show me; an implied condition is 'once you know this,' and the challenge asks what alleged partners created to merit worship.
rows.anchor: أي أعلموني وأخبروني والفاء واقعة في جواب شرط مقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing treats ماذا as a single interrogative pronoun, fronted as the object of خلق.
rows.anchor: أن يكون أسما واحدا إستفهاميا ويكون مفعولا لخلق مقدما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parsing makes ما an interrogative subject and ذا a relative predicate; the clause fills أروني's second object slot, with the relative pronoun omitted.
rows.anchor: ( ما ) وحدها أسم إستفهام مبتدأ و ( ذا )

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan notes a rarer parsing of ماذا as a single relative pronoun functioning as أروني's second object, with its antecedent omitted.
rows.anchor: فقد أستعمل كذلك على قلة على ما قال أبو حيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The turn from demanding proof to declaring manifest error ends direct argument because they cannot understand its premises or be moved by refutation.
rows.anchor: إضراب عن تبكيتهم بما ذكر إلى التسجيل عليهم بالضلال البين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them wrongdoers instead of using a pronoun shows shirk as putting things wrongly and exceeding bounds, wronging themselves through eternal punishment.
rows.anchor: ووضع الظاهر موضع ضميرهم للدلالة على أنهم بإشراكهم واضعون للشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account returns to Luqman's story to give the rest of his counsels after the opening injunction against shirk was reinforced parenthetically.
rows.anchor: رجوع إلى القصة بذكر بقية ما أريد حكايته من وصايا لقمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in إنها refers to a good or bad deed understood from context.
rows.anchor: أي الخصلة من الإساءة والإحسان لفهمها من السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes the pronoun as the matter the son asked about; a report says he asked whether God knows a mustard seed falling into the depths of the sea.
rows.anchor: أنها أي التي سألت عنها فقد روى أن لقمان سأله إبنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deed may be as tiny as a mustard seed; mithqal is a measure of weight matched by equal weight in common usage.
rows.anchor: والمثقال ما يقدر به غيره لتساوي ثقلهما وهو في العرف معلوم

rows.speaker: نافع، والأعرج، وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: Nafi, al-Araj, and Abu Jafar read مثقال in the nominative; the pronoun refers to the clause and تك is complete, with feminine agreement explained by its subject or by interpreting it as weight or a deed.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع والأعرج وأبو جعفر ( مثقال ) بالرفع على أن الضمير للقصة

words: فَتَكُن فِى صَخْرَةٍ أَوْ فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ أَوْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even at its tiniest and in a hidden, inaccessible place—the rock's interior, heaven, or earth—God will bring the deed forth.
rows.anchor: في أقصى غايات الصغر والقماءة في أخفى مكان وأحرزه كجوف الصخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view specifies the rock's interior, heaven's highest convex surface, or earth's lowest concavity; the author says the wording does not require these extremes, though emphasis may call for them.
rows.anchor: في أخفى مكان وأحرزه كجوف الصخرة أو أعلاه كمحدب السموات أو أسفله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: في may refer spatially, be used by matching expression, or carry the sense of على to express firm presence; the spatial sense remains strongest.
rows.anchor: ذكرت بحسب المكانية أو للمشاكلة أو هي بمعنى على وعبر بها

words: فِى صَخْرَةٍ أَوْ فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ أَوْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says the order begins with the familiar, hard-to-extract rock, then the more wondrous upper world, then familiar earth.
rows.anchor: بدأ بما يتعقله السامع أولا وهو كينونة الشيء في صخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One rhetorical account maps the seed's minuteness to tiny size, rock to concealment, heaven to distance, and earth's interior to darkness; no particular rock is intended.
rows.anchor: إن خفاء الشيء وصعوبة نيله بطرق بغاية صغره ويبعده عن الرائي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi identify the rock as the one on which the earth rests.
rows.anchor: وعن إبن عباس والسدي أن هذه الصخرة هي التي عليها الأرض

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas describes the earth resting on Nun, a sea, a green rock, a bull's horn, and moist earth, with only God knowing what lies beneath.
rows.anchor: وأخرج إبن مردويه عن إبن عباس أن الأرض على نون والنون على بحر والبحر

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Some identify the verse's rock with a cosmological rock in the wind; Ibn Atiyya calls such reports weakly transmitted.
rows.anchor: قال إبن عطية : وكل ذلك ضعيف لا يثبت سنده

words: فِى صَخْرَةٍ أَوْ فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ أَوْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The strongest reading is hyperbole: God's power reaches inside a rock and anywhere in heaven or earth; the cosmos lies in His grasp, so the cosmological tales should be set aside.
rows.anchor: والأقوى عندي وضع هذه الأخبار ونحوها فليست الأرض إلا في حجر الماء

rows.speaker: عبدالرحيم الجزري
rows.claim: Abd al-Rahim al-Jazari reads فتكن with kasra on kaf and a doubled, open nun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبدالرحيم الجزري ( فتكن ) بكسر الكاف وشد النون

rows.speaker: محمد بن أبي فجة البعلبكي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Abi Fajja al-Baalbakki reads فتكن with damma on ta and a doubled, open nun after fatha on kaf.
rows.anchor: وقرأ محمد بن أبي فجة البعلبكي ( فتكن ) بضم التاء وفتح الكاف

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada reads فتكن with fatha on ta, kasra on kaf, and silent nun; the same reading is also reported from al-Jazari.
rows.anchor: وقرأ قتادة ( فتكن ) بفتح التاء وكسر الكاف وسكون النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These readings derive from a bird settling in its nest, used metaphorically or by metonymy; the pronoun refers to the previously mentioned matter.
rows.anchor: من وكن الطائر إذا أستقر في وكنته أي عشه ففي الكلام إستعارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A possible alternative makes the pronoun the son: if he hides at reckoning, God brings him forth; the author says this does not fit the answer.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون للإبن والمعنى إن تختف أو تخف وقت الحساب يحضرك الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brings the deed forward for reckoning, literally or by making it present as if witnessed through mention and admission.
rows.anchor: أي يحضرها فيحاسب عليها وهذا أما على ظاهره أو المراد يجعلها كالحاضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Latif means God's knowledge reaches every hidden thing; khabir means He knows its full reality, explaining how He can bring the deed forth.
rows.anchor: إن الله لطيف ( يصل علمه تعالى إلى كل خفي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explains Latif as subtle in extracting the deed and khabir as knowing its location; another gloss calls God kind to servants and aware of hidden things, which the author dismisses.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة لطيف بإستخراجها خبير بمستقرها

words: إِن تَكُ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍۢ مِّنْ خَرْدَلٍۢ
rows.speaker: علي بن رباح اللخمي
rows.claim: Ali ibn Rabah al-Lakhmi reports that Luqman threw a mustard seed into the Yarmuk valley, waited, recalled it, and a fly brought it to his palm.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن رباح اللخمي أنه لما وعظ لقمان إبنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After commanding monotheism by forbidding shirk, Luqman alerts his son to God's complete knowledge and power.
rows.anchor: أمره بالتوحيد الذي هو أول ما يجب على المكلف في ضمن النهي عن الشرك

words: وَلَئِن سَأَلْتَهُم مَّنْ خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asked who created the heavens and earth, the polytheists answer Allah; the author prefers the implied wording 'Allah created them' over 'Allah is their creator.' Their admission is forced by obviousness.
rows.anchor: أي خلقهن الله تعالى وجوز أن يكون التقدير الله خلقهن والأول أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praise God for compelling their admission, which entails that only the true creator and benefactor deserves worship and invalidates associating others with Him.
rows.anchor: على إلزامهم وإلجائهم إلى الإعتراف بما يوجب بطلان ما هم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, praise is for making the signs of monotheism so clear that even an obstinate disputant cannot deny them.
rows.anchor: وجوز جعل المحمود عليه جعل دلائل التوحيد بحيث لا ينكرها المكابر أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most do not know that their admission obligates the conclusion; the ending elegantly extends the thought to their ignorance of why God is praised here.
rows.anchor: أن ذلك يلزمهم قيل : وفيه إيغال حسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author refers readers to his fuller discussion of the parallel in al-Ankabut 29:61.
rows.anchor: تمام الكلام في نظير الآية في العنكبوت فتذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything belongs to God by creation, ownership, and control; nothing is independent or a partner, so only He deserves worship. A possession cannot be the owner's partner or claim the owner's due.
rows.anchor: خلقا وملكا وتصرفا ليس لأحد سواه عزوجل إستقلالا ولا شركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ghani means independent of everything.
rows.anchor: إن الله هو الغني ( عن كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Hamid means deserving praise even if no one praises Him, or praised in actuality by every creature through its state.
rows.anchor: المستحق للحمد وإن لم يحمده جل وعلا أحد أو المحمود بالفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic clause answers a suspicion that God owns creation because He needs it: He is fully independent; al-Hamid signals His beneficence and perfections.
rows.anchor: وكأن الجملة جواب عما يوشك أن يخطر ببعض الأذهان السقيمة

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Tibi says the ownership statement belittles idolaters and shows God needs neither them nor their praise and worship; al-Ghani is independent of worshippers' praise, while al-Hamid means worthy of praise whether praised or not.
rows.anchor: إن قوله تعالى : ( لله ما في السموات والأرض ) تهاون بهم
